title: Accounts Assistant
description:
Accounts Assistant

Location: Swiss Cottage

Position Type: Full-Time

Department: Finance & Operations

Company Overview

Our client is a dynamic investment firm focused on identifying and managing strategic growth opportunities across diversified sectors. We are looking for a detail-oriented and proactive Accounts Assistant to join our growing finance team and support our day-to-day accounting operations.

Position Summary

The Accounts Assistant will play a key role in maintaining accurate financial records, managing transactional accounting, and supporting month-end closing processes. Working closely with the Finance Manager, you will ensure high efficiency in accounts payable, accounts receivable, and general ledger operations.

Key Responsibilities

1. Accounts Payable & Receivable
- Process, verify, and code supplier invoices and expense reports accurately.
- Prepare payment runs and manage supplier statement reconciliations.
- Issue sales invoices, monitor accounts receivable, and perform credit control follow-ups as needed.

2. Banking & Reconciliations
- Perform daily bank reconciliations across multiple accounts and currencies.
- Reconcile corporate credit cards and petty cash transactions.

3. Month-End & Financial Support
- Assist in preparing monthly trial balances, accruals, prepayments, and journal entries.
- Support the preparation of quarterly VAT/tax returns and compliance filings.
- Assist with audit preparation and liaise with external auditors as needed.

4. Administrative & Operational Finance
- Maintain clean, organized digital records and financial documentation.
- Respond promptly to internal and external accounting queries.
- Support ad-hoc financial reporting and operational projects as directed.

Qualifications & Requirements
- Education & Certifications: Degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field (or working towards AAT/ACCA/CIMA or regional equivalent qualification).
- Experience: 3 years of experience in an Accounts Assistant or Finance Administrator role (investment management or financial services background is a plus).
- Software Skills: Proficiency with accounting software
- Skills & Competencies:
- High attention to detail and strong numerical accuracy.
- Solid understanding of core bookkeeping principles.
- Strong time management and ability to prioritize tasks to meet deadlines.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

title: Credit Controller
description:
If you're the kind of Credit Controller who enjoys reducing aged debt, resolving queries and seeing the cash come in, this could be a rewarding temporary assignment.

We're recruiting a Temporary Credit Controller to support a growing business in the run-up to year-end.

Following a number of acquisitions, there's some historic debt that needs attention. Rather than simply sending standard reminders, you'll have the opportunity to get under the skin of the aged debtor report, understand what's holding up payment and improve the overall debtor position.

You'll be:

Investigating aged and historic debt
Chasing overdue balances and improving cash collection
Getting to the bottom of disputed invoices and outstanding queries
Reconciling accounts and resolving more complicated balances
Helping get the debtor ledger into better shape for year-end

If you're between roles, or simply looking for something temporary to take you through until Christmas, this could be an ideal opportunity to put your Credit Control experience to good use.

You'll need previous credit control experience and the confidence to pick up an aged ledger, understand what's sitting behind the numbers and start making progress without lots of hand-holding.

You'll be joining an existing finance team as an extra pair of experienced hands, so there'll be support around you while still giving you plenty to get your teeth into.

Like the sound of getting stuck into an aged ledger and seeing those overdue balances come down?

Apply now with your CV. If it's not up to date, don't worry. Get in touch with Natalie at Paul Card Recruitment for a confidential chat, send us your details or apply and we'll take it from there.

title: Payroll Executive
description:
Role: Payroll Executive

Location: Teesside

Salary: £28,000-£31,000 per annum

Permanent Full-time Hybrid work

Overview and Opportunity

An excellent opportunity has arisen for an experienced Payroll Executive to join a growing Payroll Services team based in Teesside.

Job description

As a Payroll Executive, you will take ownership of a portfolio of payroll clients, managing the complete payroll process from data input through to final submission, while ensuring compliance with current payroll legislation and pension requirements.

This role is ideal for a payroll professional with end-to-end payroll experience who enjoys managing their own client portfolio while delivering an accurate, compliant, and first-class payroll service.

Working within a collaborative and supportive environment, you will be responsible for the full payroll lifecycle, acting as a trusted point of contact for clients and ensuring payrolls are processed accurately and on time.

Main Responsibilities:
- Managing a portfolio of client payrolls, ensuring accurate and timely end-to-end payroll processing.
- Processing payroll changes, including new starters, leavers, salary amendments, statutory payments, pensions, and auto-enrolment.
- Calculating PAYE, National Insurance, statutory sick pay, maternity, paternity, and other statutory payments.
- Maintaining payroll records, payroll software, and employee data to ensure accuracy and compliance.
- Processing year-end payroll activities and ensuring all statutory deadlines are met.
- Managing pension administration and auto-enrolment obligations.
- Responding to payroll queries from clients and providing a professional, high-quality service.
- Producing payroll reports and journals while ensuring data accuracy throughout the payroll process.
- Keeping up to date with changes to payroll legislation, PAYE regulations, and industry best practice.
- Building strong client relationships and working collaboratively with colleagues to deliver an efficient payroll service.

Ideal Candidate:
- The successful candidate will have at least two years' end-to-end payroll experience, ideally gained within a payroll bureau or accountancy practice environment.
- Strong knowledge of UK payroll legislation, PAYE, pensions, and auto-enrolment.
- Experience managing multiple payrolls simultaneously while meeting strict deadlines.
- Excellent numerical skills with the ability to accurately calculate statutory payments.
- Confidence using payroll software, spreadsheets, and payroll reporting systems.
- Strong organisational skills with excellent attention to detail.
- Outstanding communication and customer service skills.
- The ability to work independently while contributing positively to a collaborative team.
- A proactive, flexible approach and a commitment to delivering an exceptional client experience.
